anya: FYI: new liteq int4 canary (v0.18) spike in structured-output parse errors but only for streaming. Not ZWSP this time, looks tied to ZWJ/U+200D and VS16/U+FE0F splits.
diego: Saw ~0.6% parse_fail on streaming vs 0.02% on non-streaming. Error from our json parser: 'Invalid � in input' when it hits a replacement char in the middle of a field.
noah: Minimal repro snippet (from dumped stream pieces):
```
chunk1: '{"action":"invite","name":"Tess\ud83d'
chunk2: '\udc69‍⚕️","team":"growth"}'
```
When assembled naively those halves produce surrogate escapes; the tokenizer split happened between a UTF-16 surrogate pair / zwj + vs16 sequence.
diego: This matches: token boundaries sometimes cut inside multi-codepoint emoji sequences. Quantized sampling increases boundary variance so more splits.
anya: Root cause hypothesis: streaming pieces are concatenated without ensuring valid UTF-8 codepoint boundary; incremental decoder would avoid inserting U+FFFD.
noah: Quick mitigation idea: use codecs.IncrementalDecoder('utf-8') at stream assembly so we defer decoding until we have a full codepoint. Pseudocode:```python
dec = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
text = dec.decode(byte_chunk, final=False)
# text will be '' if chunk ends mid-codepoint; keep internal buffer in decoder
```
anya: Agreed. Also add a lightweight check: if json.loads fails and '�' present -> retry with incremental reassemble then run `unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)` and remove stray ZWJ (U+200D) only if it's isolated (not part of known multi-codepoint sequences).
diego: Need to be careful: removing ZWJ can change emoji meaning. Better: on parse fail, request non-streaming replay from model to get canonical payload before invoking downstream tool.
noah: That could be costly at scale. Proposal: first attempt incremental reassembly repair locally; if still fails, then fallback to non-streaming replay with idempotency headers.
anya: Telemetry: capture "stream_boundary_offset", "last_byte_hex", and "decoder_pending_bytes" when a parse error occurs. Tag metrics with quant_profile (int4) and model.
noah: I'll add a canary test that injects multi-codepoint emojis and VS16 sequences into prompts and asserts no parse_fail after repair.
qa-bot: Canary injection plan scheduled: 5k streaming calls with emoji-heavy prompts, compare parse_fail rate vs baseline.
diego: Also add token id neighborhood dump (5 tokens before/after boundary) for correlation. Might reveal tokenizer rules that cut in the middle of grapheme clusters.
anya: Short term runtime behavior: on structured parse fail -> (1) incremental reassemble + sanitize attempt, (2) if still failing -> automatic non-streaming replay with X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency header, (3) if replay succeeds, continue; else soft-fail response.
noah: Tests: unit test for incremental decoder behaviour, integration for replay dedupe, and load canary.
anya: I'll open PR with incremental decoder wrapper + metric tags + canary harness changes. Assigning myself.
diego: I'll add token neighborhood telemetry and metric alerts.
noah: I'll own the replay/dedupe implementation.
infra-bot: Scheduled deploy: streaming-utf8-fix v0.18.3 -> staging at 23:45 UTC.
anya: After staging smoke, run 5k targeted canary and post results here.
noah: Added low-priority follow-up: run fp16 vs int4 tokenization diffs on same prompts to quantify split increase.
anya: Action items recap: (1) PR incremental decoder + tests (anya), (2) token-id dump telemetry (diego), (3) replay + idempotency (noah), (4) canary run + report (qa-bot/noah).
anya: will update with PR link and eta. :white_check_mark:
